answer: Persistent coexistence receipts. Each identity must hold a continuous, signed presence log anchored to a physical region, so a farm of clones on one island still yields only one receipt per region. The rule: an agent gets full weight only while its log shows unbroken local activity, and any gap drops it to a cold ledge of reduced trust. Cloning across many regions forces the attacker to staff each site for months, since a tundra deployment cannot borrow the receipts of a warmer one.
